note: Unconditional access to ctxt->pushTab when ctxt->sax2 is 0. pushTab is only allocated inside nameNsPush, which is only called when sax2 is true. With a SAX1 handler (initialized=1), sax2 remains 0, so pushTab is NULL and this dereference causes a NULL pointer crash.

code: xmlFatalErrMsgStrIntStr(ctxt, XML_ERR_TAG_NOT_FINISHED, "Premature end of data in tag %s line %d\n", name, line, NULL);
note: The line value read from the NULL pushTab is used in the fatal error message, confirming the bad-cast/read from invalid memory.

xmlDetectSAX2 sets ctxt->sax2=1 only if ctxt->sax->initialized == XML_SAX2_MAGIC. A user-supplied SAX1 handler (initialized=1) leaves sax2=0, yet xmlParseElement is still invoked unconditionally later in this function.
Called regardless of sax2 value. When sax2=0, xmlParseElement reaches the pushTab dereference at line 9962 if the document ends prematurely inside an element.
When sax2=0, the content parser uses the SAX1 path and never calls nameNsPush, so pushTab remains NULL throughout parsing.
Confirms that nameNsPush (which allocates pushTab) is only invoked in the sax2=1 branch. With sax2=0, pushTab is never allocated.
Entry point. The function assumes pushTab is valid because it is only reached via the sax2 path in normal usage, but the caller does not enforce sax2.
Parses element content. If the input ends prematurely (CUR==0 after content), the code proceeds to the vulnerable pushTab access.
Trigger condition: premature end of data inside an element. This is satisfied by an XML document that opens a tag but never closes it.
Reads the element name from nameTab, which is valid. The subsequent pushTab read at line 9962 is the crash point.
